construct: Trauma-informed care emphasizes safety, trustworthiness, collaboration, empowerment, voice, and choice. During potentially triggering examinations, clinicians should explain what will happen, seek permission before contact, offer reasonable choices/supports, and make clear that the patient can pause or stop the examination at any time.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Trauma-informed examination technique preserves safety and patient control through explanation, permission before contact, choices about pacing and support, and explicit ability to pause or stop.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: A chaperone is a legitimate supportive measure and therefore the strongest distractor, but it does not substitute for ongoing consent, choice, and control of the examination.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only the keyed approach simultaneously provides transparency, permission, choices, and ongoing ability to halt the examination.
